Name: test_apply_coupon_scenario_from_json[free shipping only coupon]
Description:
Apply each eligible JSON-defined Coupon and verify the Order totals.

The test checks that the scenario's derived product price meets its
minimum spend and that the JSON expected discount matches the configured
discount rule before comparing those expectations with the API response.

Name: test_create_order_with_malformed_line_items
Description:
Reject an Order payload whose line_items field is not a list.

WooCommerce expects line_items to be an array of line-item objects. This
test sends a string to exercise request-schema validation before a valid
Order can be created.

Name: test_create_order_with_invalid_status
Description:
Reject an Order creation request with an unsupported status.

Test flow:

    1. Create a valid Product to satisfy the Order line-item requirement.
    2. Send an Order payload with an unsupported status.
    3. Verify HTTP 400 and the WooCommerce error response contract.

Name: test_coupon_application_rejected_below_minimum[percentage-below-minimum]
Description:
Reject applying a Coupon when the Order is below its minimum spend.

The Order is created without a Coupon and registered by create_valid_order.
The negative operation updates that existing Order, so the resource
remains owned by the fixture even when WooCommerce rejects the Coupon.

Name: test_create_order_for_registered_customer
Description: Create an Order for an existing Customer and verify its association.

Name: test_reject_coupon_scenario_below_minimum_from_json[percentage coupon below minimum]
Description:

A valid Order is created before applying the Coupon. The expected failure
therefore leaves an Order registered with the shared cleanup lifecycle.

Name: test_get_nonexistent_order
Description:
Validate the not-found response when retrieving an unknown Order ID.

No setup resource is required because the unknown ID is the scenario under
test.

Test flow:
    1. Request an Order ID that does not exist.
    2. Assert that the GET operation returns HTTP 404.
    3. Validate the WooCommerce not-found error contract.
